biography.text: Aḥmad ibn Mūsā ibn Shākir was one of the three brothers known collectively as the Banū Mūsā, active in ninth-century Baghdad. Reference accounts associate him particularly with mechanics and ḥiyal, while warning that the brothers' works often cannot be assigned confidently to one individual. This dossier examines that attribution boundary rather than attempting a complete biography.
gaps: Compare early biographical notices and individual records before adding personal dates, education, or a distinct career narrative.

timeline.text: Sources place Aḥmad in the ninth-century Baghdad milieu but do not establish a secure personal birth or death year in this batch. The surviving copies are later manuscript witnesses, not composition dates.
gaps: Review the original biographical notices for a defensible personal chronology.

fields.text: Iranica calls the Kitāb al-ḥiyal Aḥmad's only surviving work. Hill's publisher-hosted digest of earlier sources reports the earliest cited Fihrist attribution collectively to the Banū Mūsā, a later account emphasizing Aḥmad's particular skill in ḥiyal, and further collective descriptions. ISMI and the 1979 edition record the work under the Banū Mūsā; TDV warns that individual authorship across their corpus generally cannot be determined with certainty. The evidence supports Aḥmad's association with mechanics while leaving the exact authorship of the extant compilation under review.
gaps: Collate the early Arabic and Syriac notices directly; Hill's 1979 account is an intermediary.
Read the full Hill introduction and al-Ḥassan's Arabic edition; compare the title pages, colophons, and internal divisions of the six ISMI-listed witnesses.

legacy.text: Aḥmad is associated with mechanical ḥiyal, while the surviving book is transmitted and catalogued as a Banū Mūsā work. This evidence does not prove that he alone composed the whole compilation or invented every device. Collective reception and individual expertise remain separate claims.
gaps: Trace influence through identifiable texts and transmission evidence, not resemblance alone.

investigations.title: Aḥmad's individual association with the collectively transmitted Kitāb al-ḥiyal
investigations.field: History of technology / authorship and transmission
investigations.historicalProblem: How do early historical notices, modern references, and manuscript catalogues distinguish Aḥmad's role in ḥiyal from authorship of the extant Kitāb al-ḥiyal?
investigations.historicalContext: The Banū Mūsā are frequently described collectively, while specialist accounts also distinguish individual expertise. Hill's 1979 edition makes earlier attribution notices accessible in English; reference works phrase authorship differently.
investigations.method: Compare Hill's publisher preview of reported medieval notices with Iranica's individual attribution, collective author fields in ISMI and the edition record, and TDV's explicit caution about allocating authorship within the brothers' corpus.
investigations.observationsOrCalculations: No device passage or mechanism is reconstructed. ISMI lists six witnesses; Hill's publisher preview identifies three major manuscripts and two fragments.
investigations.reportedResult: Hill reports a collective Fihrist attribution and a later account singling out Aḥmad's skill in ḥiyal. Iranica calls the work Aḥmad's, while modern catalogue and edition records use the group attribution; TDV explicitly cautions that individual authorship is uncertain across the corpus. Aḥmad's association with mechanics is supported; sole authorship of the extant compilation remains unresolved.
investigations.whatWasNew: No invention or priority claim is made. The batch documents the difference between individual expertise and the work's collective transmission.
investigations.limitations: The early historical texts and Arabic edition were not directly collated; neither were manuscript title pages, colophons, or internal divisions. Hill's preview is an intermediary digest.
investigations.laterInfluence: Not assessed in this authorship-focused batch.
